title: Yellowed Dense Chaozhou Chicken Dumplings
description: A sour and dense Chinese dish featuring almond flour, perfect for a diabetic-friendly date night, with a unique Chaozhou twist.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine chicken, almond flour, cornstarch, salt, and white pepper, and mix well.
Add rice vinegar, scallions, sesame oil, and water to the bowl, and mix until a dense dough forms.
Wrap the dough in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into small balls, about 1 inch in diameter.
Flatten each ball into a disk shape, and place a small spoonful of sour mustard in the center of each disk.
Fold the dough over the filling, and press the edges together to seal the dumpling.
Place the dumplings in a single layer in a sous-vide bag, and seal the bag.
Cook the dumplings in a water bath at 180 degrees Fahrenheit for 30 minutes.
Remove the dumplings from the bag, and serve hot with your favorite dipping sauce.
Brush the tops of the dumplings with beaten egg for a golden glaze.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
